plan: [Use the symmetric Bayes–Nash equilibrium for a first-price sealed-bid with n=3 and values iid Uniform[0,49]. Optimal bid b(v) = (n-1)/n * v = 2/3 v. For v=23, b = 15.333... Round to nearest $0.1 -> $15.3. This maximizes long-run expected profit.]

[With three symmetric bidders and values iid uniform, the first-price sealed-bid Bayesian equilibrium is to shade your bid to (n-1)/n * v. Here (2/3)*18 = 12. Bid 12.0 (valid at $0.1 increments). This maximizes expected profit given no prior history; ties are random so 12 is appropriate.]

[Three bidders, independent private values, no history. For a first-price sealed-bid auction with n=3 and uniform values, the symmetric equilibrium is b(v)=(n-1)/n * v = 2/3*v. With v=39, bid = 2/3*39 = 26.0. Round to the nearest $0.1. This balances winning probability and payment to maximize expected surplus given no prior info about opponents.]
